is in S8's working block and in S9's committed block" (`corridor.test.ts:129`). It uses P23's geometry: way:1

batch. It reads kerb() on the open overlay for the faces at (3000,1000) and (1000,3000). It asserts that the blocks

* Real code: green (M00 above, and the tree's near run below).

* The same fixture now kills K06 (turn-away treated as a corner) and K36 (splice threshold 4·minEdge). Both fail on
  this test, which closes note 2 (note 17).

**B-2 — fixed.** The listed test "a face with no bounding spine: kerb(F) = F, and corridorUnion leaves it one built
block …" (`kerb.test.ts:42`) gained a holed face: the frame's face round an inner `district_bound` ring that declares no
half-width. It asserts that kerb(F) is the outer ring counter-clockwise plus the hole clockwise (`:69`), that this equals
F's rings by normal forms and by area (`:73 – 74`), and that corridorUnion returns `whole: [g]` with no kerb edge
(`:76 – 80`).
* Real code: green.
* K37 (a spine-less face returns `[outer]` only): `K37 exit=1 KILLED … 'Tests 1 failed | 17 passed (18)'`, failing at

## Verdict: FAIL — two blockers, both a listed test whose fixture cannot see a surviving mutant on its promise

The code is sound on every path the seat probed: one `kerb` function, every gate green, both near runs at PR size
green, the oracle agreements green with their guards, the own-refusal cap at 0, and the related reds traced to
insertChain by a control. The two blockers are test gaps, each closed by one fixture:

* **B-1** — §13.2's S8 ≡ S9 test (`corridor.test.ts:93`) has no face whose junction makes `readKerb` splice a split
  end into kerb(F). Mutant K25 (`kerb()` returns the unspliced `kerbOf` ring — a second kerb for S8) survives every test,
  and it breaks the contract on a reachable face (probe P23, CONFIRMED).
* **B-2** — the listed test "a face with no bounding spine: kerb(F) = F" (`kerb.test.ts:41`) uses a face with no hole.
  Mutant K37 (a spine-less face's kerb drops its holes) survives every test, and kerb(F) ≠ F on a holed face (probe P1,
  CONFIRMED).

Sixteen minor notes are in `checks/M0-a-09-notes.md` for M4. They include the KI row the author asked the checker to
copy: the dangling antenna, N-45 (C-0212 (8), C-0218 (5)).

## (6) Probes (own mirror, CONFIRMED unless marked)

* **P1.** On a spine-less face with a hole, kerb = `["0,0 4000,0 4000,4000 0,4000","1000,1000 1000,3000 3000,3000 3000,1000"]`
  with area2 `32000000` and `-8000000` (the hole is clockwise), and corridorUnion leaves the face whole. That is right.
  K37's result, the outer ring alone, is kerb(F) ≠ F (B-2).
* **P9.** A ring way round a square: the holed outer face and the inner face, both banded. They tile exactly. The inner
  block is `1300,1300 … 2700,2700` (sharp corners). The outer kerb area is 9 319 848 cm² against the rounded-square
  analytic 9 317 257; the 2 591 cm² gap is the inscribed chords' deficit, within 2 cm sagitta. The blocks' area equals
  the kerbs'. There are no splits.
* **P12.** A face narrower than its two bands: kerb `ok([])`, corridorUnion `wholeBand`.
* **P5.** A crossing with one half-width of 20 cm (below `attractCm`). The kerb is attracted onto the spine, and the
  band faces are all classed wedges (strips 0). The arena is healthy and tiles. Note 9.
* **P4.** Determinism: 2 000 random networks built twice and banded in opposite face orders. All 1 998 committed pairs
  gave identical `state` and an identical `BandResult`. (The `it` hit vitest's 5 s default timeout after the property
  had finished and printed; that timeout is the probe's.)
* **P20 / P23.** Two ways meeting end to end at a bend (F turns away at J). Real code: one split from J to the nearest
  kerb point, the arena healthy, and kerb() ≡ the committed block. On the slanted variant (way:1 (0,1700)–(2100,2050)
  half-width 310, way:2 (2100,2050)–(2600,4000) half-width 270, face at (3000,1000)), readKerb splices the split end
  (2308,1823) into the round join. The unspliced `kerbOf` ring lacks it, so with K25 in place the committed block ≠
  kerb() (`blocks==spliced false`).
* **P22.** 223 straight-through T-junctions on random slanted spines. kerb() equals the unspliced kerbOf in all 223,
  and the committed blocks equal kerb() in all 223. So the existing fixtures never reach the splice.
* **P3.** tileRings agreement, 10⁴ cases. There were 3 attracted overlap refusals, each where an oracle result has a
  hole. No unjustified refusal hides in the judge's unconditional acceptance of attracted refusals (note 6).
* **P21.** The corridor agreement's 416 `input-refused` cases. 366 are the judge's chord leaving its own frame
  (`E_LEVEL a new edge of an L1 batch lies outside …`, the chord reach diag + 400 against a 20 000 cm margin); 4 are a
  ring way the arena refused as branching; 2 are the tunnel fixture's frame out of range; 2 are no face found. These
  are generator losses, not the operation's (note 7).

## (7) Failing lines and required changes

**B-1 — §13.2's S8 ≡ S9 test cannot see a second kerb on a splice-producing junction.**
* *Evidence.* Mutant K25 (kerb.ts:345: `kerb()` returns `kerbOf(readFace(…))` without `readKerb`'s splices) survives
  all 33 near tests at 1000. The random-network property and B-FUZZ use straight frame-to-frame chords, and the
  agreement uses a ring way plus a straight chord, so neither can produce a turn-away junction (PLAUSIBLE that it also
  survives at PR size, by the generators' construction). P23 (CONFIRMED) gives the geometry: on the face at
  (3000, 1000) beside way:1 (0,1700)–(2100,2050) half-width 310 and way:2 (2100,2050)–(2600,4000) half-width 270, the
  real code commits a block equal to kerb() on the open overlay. Under K25, kerb() lacks the spliced vertex (2308,1823),
  and the block S9 commits ≠ the kerb S8 reads. That breaks §4.6 / §13.2's Hausdorff 0 and the item's checker clause
  (no second kerb).
* *Required change.* Add to the §13.2 test, or beside it in `corridor.test.ts`, a face whose junction makes `readKerb`
  splice the split end into kerb(F): a turn-away junction between two ways meeting at a bend on slanted lines, such as
  P23's. Assert kerb(F) read on the open L1 overlay ≡ the committed blocks, by normal forms. It is green on the real
  code and red under K25 (the seat's P23 shows both). The same fixture can pin C-0212 (4)'s turn-away split (K06) and
  the splice threshold (K36).

**B-2 — the spine-less test cannot see a kerb that drops F's holes.**
* *Evidence.* Mutant K37 (kerb.ts:274 – 276: a spine-less face returns `[outer]` only) survives all 33 near tests at
  1000. Neither `kerb.test.ts:41` nor `guard.test.ts`'s `limit/one-item-kerb-no-spine` face has a hole, and B-FUZZ's
  faces have none. P1 (CONFIRMED): on a district-bounded face with an inner district-bound ring, the real kerb is outer
  + clockwise hole (area2 32 000 000 and −8 000 000). K37 returns the outer ring alone, which is kerb(F) ≠ F — S8 would
  plan cuts across the hole.
* *Required change.* Add a spine-less face with a hole (an inner closed chain declaring no half-width) to the listed
  test. Assert that kerb(F) equals F's rings, holes included, and that corridorUnion leaves the face one built block.
